title: Reusable Instruction Libraries — Brainlet
body:
Short pitch
- Problem: teams keep reauthoring similar instruction blocks across flows (customer support, sales assistant, code gen). Leads to drift, duplicated QA, inconsistent outputs.
- Idea: a sharable, versioned library of instruction fragments (short instructions, examples, constraints) that can be referenced/embedded at runtime by templates or the API.

Context and why now
- hosting API customers asking for consistency controls + easier prompt governance.
- Optimize for: auditability, reuse, small ops overhead.
- Distinct from full prompt-store: focus on small, composable instruction units that can be combined dynamically.

Goals (success criteria)
- Developer UX: create and reference instruction fragments easily in SDK and console (goal: <10s to add reference in a prompt template).
- Operational: versioned fragments with changelog + ability to pin model invocations to a fragment version.
- Quality: reduce prompt duplication by 50% in pilot teams across 8 weeks.
- Govern: RBAC for who can publish default library items; audit log for usage.
- Cost/latency: negligible added latency (instructions are just text inserted or referenced server-side).

Core concepts / terminology
- Fragment: a short instruction or example (one paragraph, or a couple of few-shot examples).
- Template: existing prompt template system that can reference fragments by id and version.
- Library: collection of fragments with tags/profile metadata.
- Binding: runtime resolution of fragment references to a specific version.

User stories (rough)
- As an engineer, I want to create a fragment "apology + ask for clarification" and reference it in multiple prompt templates so that support flows sound consistent.
- As a platform admin, I want to pin the stable v2 of the "sensitive-data-safeguard" fragment for prod so rollouts don't accidentally pick up breaking edits.
- As an evaluator, I want to run diff tests between fragment versions to see output variance on a set of eval prompts.

UX/Console ideas (quick)
- Library page: list + search + filter by tag/team. Inline preview + copy sample usage.
- Fragment editor: edit text with small metadata: description, author, tags, stability (experimental/approved), examples.
- Template editor: autocompletion on "@fragment:" that inserts reference skeleton; hover shows preview and version dropdown.
- Usage map: which templates/routes reference fragment X.

API/SDK considerations
- POST /fragments -> returns id + version. PATCH -> creates new version. GET /fragments/{id}?version=2 -> returns patched text.
- Runtime reference resolution: a template can include {{fragment:foo:latest}} or {{fragment:foo:v3}}. The resolve happens server-side before sending to model.
- Security: resolve only within same org/namespace; allow cross-org imports with explicit consent.

Rollout plan (MVP -> next)
- MVP (4 wks): CRUD fragments in console + API, template reference resolution for hosted prompts, basic search, pin to version.
- Next (8 wks): RBAC, audit logs, diffs & eval hooks, SDK helpers, batch replace in templates.
- Later: shared library marketplace (internal), fragment-level metrics (per-token cost, avg latency delta), automatic suggestions from eval regressions.

Technical notes / pitfalls
- Fragment substitution should preserve tokenization expectations. If we insert a large fragment, it changes token counts + might affect batching heuristics. Need to model token delta and surface cost estimate in console.
- For streaming: if we resolve server-side we can stream normally; if fragments are fetched at runtime from remote (cross-region) must cache locally at serving node to avoid latency spikes.
- Version pinning vs latest: default to pinned version for production templates to avoid accidental regressions.
- Caching: fragments can be small; keep in config cache (in-memory) keyed by fragment id+ver with TTL. Add invalidation hooks when published.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Should fragments support structured objects (JSON instructions) in addition to text? Pro: better for tool-calling and structured outputs. Con: increases complexity for storage and preview.
- Who gets to publish org-default fragments? Suggest: team leads + platform reviewers. Need workflow for propose -> review -> approve.
- QA/evals: how to tie fragment changes to regressions across templates that combine fragments? Might need a "fragment smoke test" harness.

Notes to self / TODOs
- Persona examples to draft: support-apology, code-formatter-rules, legal-disclaimer-short, safety-biasing-snippet.
- Mock console screens: library list, fragment editor, template insertion UX (I can sketch on whiteboard Wed).
- Ask Asha about linking fragment audit logs to existing observability (console tracing).
- Slack: start a quick poll in #product-early to gauge interest for cross-team library sharing.

Rough POA for demo (target internal demo in 3 weeks)
- Build minimal fragment CRUD + insertion into an existing support template + show version pinning and a small regression test that highlights change impact.
- Demo script: create fragment -> inject in template -> generate before/after using v1 then publish v2 -> show pinned template still uses v1, unpinned uses v2, run eval on 10 canned prompts -> show diff.

Freeform brainstorm snippets (choppy)
- Could we auto-suggest fragments from telemetry? detect repeated prefixes in prompts and propose them as fragment candidates.
- Use fragments to power 'role' presets for chat (System: tone+constraints fragment).
- Allow fragments to include variables ({{client_name}}) that are interpolated at runtime from template context. Need to restrict eval to safe vars.

Final quick wins (low effort)
- Add a console page listing top 20 duplicated prompt blocks across org and allow 1-click convert -> fragment and replace.
- Expose fragment usage graph so teams can find shared infra and reduce duplication.

-- end brainlet --

(Informal — half-baked, lots to tidy. Harboring this as a personal scratch; will turn into a PRD outline if positive early signals.)
